key_insight: Relay contact welding can silently compromise student-built emergency-stop circuits despite successful commissioning tests.
engineering_relevance: Workshop safety assurance should include monitoring sensitive to welded contacts rather than rely solely on initial functional testing.
method: Model the circuit as a series safety function degraded by contact welding.
Identify conditions where welded contacts cause an undetected failure to stop.
Simulate before-after-control-impact evaluations across cluster counts and effect sizes.
evidence_signal: Using 2,000 replications per design cell, the analysis estimated that detecting a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power requires 54 clusters.
watch_item: The power estimates depend on assumed variance parameters, and the abstract reports no direct field validation of injury-risk reduction.
paper_title: Functional-Safety-Integrity Degradation of Student-Built Emergency-Stop Circuits in Engineering Technology Education Workshops: A Fault-Injection Evaluation Linking Relay Contact Welding to Operator Injury-Risk Exposure
